title: Work Map writer concurrency policy parity

phases.objective: Align the governed automation-overlap resource group with the workflow-dispatch-only Work Map sole-writer concurrency identity already present on current main.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The overlap analyzer loads the repository workflow inventory and the governed resource-group policy on the exact candidate head.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The Work Map writer concurrency key exactly matches its policy resource group, cancellation remains disabled, and the real-repository overlap regression reports zero critical findings.
steps: Load the workflow-dispatch-only spec-kit-work-map-autofix workflow from the exact candidate tree.
Load the governed pull-request-work-map-generated-artifacts resource group.
Compare the workflow concurrency group with the policy-required concurrency group.
Execute the focused automation-overlap analyzer regression against the real repository inventory.
Require zero blocking findings without suppressing behavioral high-severity observations.
assertions: The required concurrency group equals spec-kit-work-map-artifacts-${{ github.repository }}-${{ inputs.branch }}.
The sole Work Map writer remains the only write member of its resource group.
No behavioral finding is allowlisted or downgraded by this change.
No repository content write, protected-ref mutation, Production action, deployment, provider call, credential read, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, external send, or force push is performed.

phases.objective: Observe the aligned policy during one governed Work Map writer dispatch and one unrelated workflow-only pull request.
Reject future Work Map trigger or concurrency changes unless workflow and policy are updated atomically.
Prove Draft and Ready Automation Overlap Guard cycles with zero critical findings on an exact current-main candidate.
Keep the permanent overlap ratchet aligned with the sole-writer contract without granting execution or deployment authority.
